findings.reason: §4 and §5 would cite the built supervisor as the thing the re-hold path starts and drop the framing that the launcher must be built, which is the largest piece of §4/§5 work as written.
findings.text: §4's launcher design (the batch step starts the zellij server, the private runtime directory carries every session's sockets, a login node can only attach a viewer, a session runs as its own reaped step) is already implemented by `fleet_supervisor.py` plus `bin/fleet-claude` (`FLEET_SESSION_STEPS=1` runs the pane's Claude as its own `srun --overlap --pty --jobid` step; the default runs it under the batch step) and `bin/fleet-attach` (viewer step, detach-safe), committed 2026-09-28 and refined 2026-10-03; the plan names no reckon module and searches only the imas-ambix note and the sibling plan.

findings.reason: it decides whether §5 extends `fleet_supervisor.py` or forks a shell launcher, and the honest change is the extension the plan should name.
findings.text: the plan requires the re-hold path to "create the batch script that starts the zellij server" and never says why the existing batch step (`bin/fleet-supervisor` running `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`, already the allocation's batch step) cannot carry the zellij server, so the re-hold extension is left ambiguous between extending the existing batch step and writing a second launcher script.

findings.reason: a second cgroup-resolution path can disagree with the one that gates placement and nested launch, and the owner already distinguishes the login-node user slice from the job cgroup, which is exactly the two-sided read the plan asks for.
findings.text: §5 reports the throttled fraction "read from whichever cgroup is running them, naming the counter file on each side", but the resolution of the process's own cgroup is already owned by `reckon/crew/summary._user_slice_dir` (with `LOGIN_CGROUP_ROOT` / `SELF_CGROUP_PATH`) and composed by `reckon/host.host_facts`, which `reckon/nested_launch.py` and `reckon/crew/placement.py` already read to answer "in allocation"; the plan names neither and would re-derive the path.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module of its own; the behaviour it describes is carried by one existing deep module (`fleet_supervisor.py`, 1355 lines) rather than a spread of shallow wrappers, so there is nothing shallow to flag.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan resolves "whichever cgroup is running them" for the throttled-fraction measurement, a resolution already owned by `reckon/crew/summary._user_slice_dir` and composed by `reckon/host.host_facts`, which the plan does not name.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched imas-ambix's `login-node-storage-contention` note and the sibling plan `the-fleet-shares-one-allocation`, but the launcher is already implemented in `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py` and `bin/fleet-claude` / `bin/fleet-attach`, which the plan names nowhere.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 requires the re-hold path "create the batch script that starts the zellij server" without recognising that `fleet_supervisor.py` already is that batch step, so the plan invites a parallel shell launcher beside the module it should extend.
